entries.test: Representative audits of Facebook feeds around publication would establish whether AI-generated content dominated what users saw.
entries.note: The surrounding passage identifies Facebook as the platform.

entries.test: Public audits of false or misleading AI-generated content and its production and distribution through Google and Microsoft would test the claimed contamination and substantial facilitation.
entries.note: The subsequent examples give pollution a concrete reading involving false information and fabricated images.

entries.test: Public evaluations of provenance technologies and content detection, alongside audits of exposure to AI-generated content, would test the claimed lack of reliable alternatives to human scrutiny and resulting unavoidability.
entries.note: The statement explicitly explains unavoidability through an asserted absence of reliable provenance methods.
The passage supplies no shared criterion for what would constitute repairing the internet. Persistent false content and irreparable damage to the internet are different claims.

entries.test: Whether AI-generated falsehoods and fabricated images are durably eliminated from the web would test the prediction of their continued persistence.
entries.note: This is a firm prediction with no deadline; continued presence alone cannot establish permanence.
The absolute assertion concerns the companies' private consideration of consequences. Public conduct cannot establish a complete absence of such consideration.

entries.test: Industry financial disclosures, financing obligations, operating economics, and environmental impact studies would test the asserted over-leverage, lack of a viable route to profitability, billion-dollar losses, and environmental harm.
entries.note: The profitability assertion concerns economic viability at publication, rather than a dated prediction.
The source says he 'would' do these things; the proposition changes this into ongoing conduct. The passage is an exaggerated character denunciation.
Zitron extends the denunciation to both men, but the proposition converts asserted willingness into actual ongoing spending.
Calling the features useless and detrimental expresses an assessment of their worth without an agreed performance criterion.
'Change things' identifies no shared observable outcome that would distinguish fulfillment from failure.

entries.test: Documented reversals of the criticized company practices attributable to informed public pressure would test the predicted forced change.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supplies the relevant practices. Public pressure is presented as the mechanism, rather than an explicit hypothetical antecedent.

entries.test: OpenAI's annual financial reporting, operating economics, and studies of its software's environmental impact would test the claimed $5 billion annual burn, unsustainability, and environmental damage.
entries.note: OpenAI is a reasonable contextual referent, but 'harms' weakens the source's 'destroys the environment.'

entries.test: Public training-data records, licensing agreements, and copyright litigation findings would establish whether OpenAI built its software through large-scale unauthorized appropriation of creative works.
entries.note: The plain factual allegation concerns appropriation of creative works; 'larceny' need not be read as a precise criminal charge.
This record captures the recommendation to readers. Its embedded factual allegations can be assessed separately.
